About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About The Role
We’re looking for a Technical Program Manager who can work across engineering, product, and business teams. You’ll bring the technical judgment to earn engineers’ trust and the ability to create clarity and momentum across complex programs. This is a hands-on role with executive visibility and direct impact on how Ramp’s engineering organization scales.


You’re energized by complexity and curious about how AI can improve the way engineering teams work. You experiment with AI tools yourself, understand how they are changing software development, and bring that perspective to the programs you lead.

What You’ll Do

  • Lead large technical programs across engineering and partner teams, from infrastructure scaling to reliability and incident response.

  • Connect platform and product engineering teams, keep context flowing, surface dependencies, and drive effective execution.

  • Own programs from scoping and kickoff through delivery, measurement, and retrospective.

  • Partner with engineering leaders on roadmaps, identify how projects overlap or depend on one another, and keep programs aligned with organizational goals.

  • Help engineers, engineering managers, and partner teams communicate business and engineering priorities across the organization.

  • Strengthen Ramp’s incident response program by improving processes, facilitating retrospectives, and helping teams act on what they learn.

  • Help define how TPMs work at Ramp by setting standards, creating playbooks, and improving program practices.

What You’ll Need

  • 5+ years of technical program management experience, ideally in a high-growth startup.

  • Hands-on fluency with AI tools such as Cursor or Claude Code, and a point of view on how they can improve day-to-day work and software development.

  • The ability to execute directly while improving how the broader team works.

  • A track record of building trust quickly and working effectively across teams.

  • A BA/BS in computer science, engineering, information systems, analytics, or another technical or analytical field.

  • Strong systems thinking: you can connect architecture, product, compliance, and timelines, and spot risks early.

  • Experience leading cross-functional programs toward ambitious goals with urgency and ownership.

Nice To Haves

  • Experience with cell-based or multi-region architectures, or international expansion.

  • Hands-on experience with infrastructure, CI/CD, or observability tools.

  • Experience leading reliability programs.

  • Experience building programs in rigorous, fast-moving organizations.

  • A background in software engineering.

  • Familiarity with how LLM-based systems are built and deployed, enough to have substantive conversations with the engineers building them.

Ramp is hiring its first dedicated Physical Security Lead to build and run the program that protects our people, our leaders, our events, and our offices. Our footprint now spans a multi-floor New York headquarters, Ramp-managed offices, and a growing set of hubs across North America and Europe. Our leaders are increasingly visible on public stages.

You'll own three areas in roughly equal measure: executive protection, event security, and office security (access control, cameras, guards, and building security). Your job is to turn a set of strong vendors and partner teams into one measurable, risk-based program.

This is a high-ownership IC role on the Corporate Security team. It reports to the Director of IT & Corporate Security and is based at our NYC HQ. This is a physical security role; cybersecurity and information security are owned by other Ramp security teams. We aren't looking for a guard supervisor or a box-checker. We want someone who makes it safe for Ramp to move fast, host great events, and keep our leaders accessible.

What You'll Do

  • Build and run Ramp's executive protection program:

    • Protective risk assessments and residential security reviews.

    • Domestic and international travel security.

    • Advance work for high-visibility appearances.

    • Selecting, standing up, and managing our executive protection provider.

  • Turn threat intelligence into protective action. Partner with Detection & Response to move from online threat and exposure monitoring to threat assessments, personal-information exposure reduction, and clear escalation playbooks.

  • Own security for internal and external events, from all-hands and offsites to conferences, customer events, and executive dinners:

    • Risk-tiered intake and written security plans.

    • Coordination with venues and vendors.

    • On-site leadership for the highest-risk events.

    • After-action reviews.

  • Set Ramp's global physical security standards for access control, video surveillance, intercoms, visitor management, and alarm monitoring. Tier them for headquarters, Ramp-managed offices, and flexible or serviced hub spaces.

  • Build security into every new office, move, and expansion:

    • Write the security design requirements and review drawings.

    • Manage integrators through installation and acceptance testing.

    • Partner with IT on network and identity integration.

  • Manage the guard program and security vendors end to end: scope, post orders, SLAs and KPIs, budget, and quarterly business reviews. Own the security relationship with landlords and building management.

  • Lead emergency preparedness and physical incident response:

    • Emergency notifications, evacuation and shelter-in-place plans, and drills.

    • Liaison with local law enforcement.

    • Workplace-violence prevention, in partnership with People and Legal.

  • Run physical access governance with IT. Tie access to joiner/mover/leaver events, run regular access reviews, and keep audit-ready evidence for physical security controls.

  • Measure and report program health to leadership. Use AI and automation to scale the program without scaling headcount.

What You Need

  • 6+ years in corporate or physical security, including 3+ years owning a security program or major workstream at a multi-site company. Executing someone else's program doesn't count toward this.

  • Hands-on depth in at least two of the three areas (executive protection, event security, physical security systems such as access control and cameras) and solid working knowledge of the third.

  • Experience administering or deploying enterprise access control and video platforms (e.g., Avigilon Alta/Openpath, Verkada, Genetec, LenelS2), and partnering with IT on networking and SSO.

  • A track record of managing security vendors (guard, protection, integrator, event staffing) through contracts, SLAs, budgets, and performance reviews.

  • Strong risk judgment. You size controls to the actual threat, explain the tradeoffs, and lead with "here's how we do this safely" rather than "no."

  • Excellent writing. You can produce a crisp SOP, an event security plan, and a one-page executive brief.

  • Willingness to work from our NYC office 4 days a week, travel 10–15%, support occasional evening and weekend events, and serve as primary on-call for physical security incidents (with the Director as backup and guard and vendor partners as on-site first response).

  • Real, day-to-day use of AI tools in your work.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience at a high-growth tech, fintech, or financial services company with a high-profile founder or CEO.

  • Experience writing security design standards for office buildouts and reading architectural or low-voltage drawings.

  • A government protective, law enforcement, or military background, combined with corporate program ownership.

  • An established network of protection, event security, and integrator vendors in NYC, SF, and internationally.

  • This is a builder role. Parts of the program exist today (vendors, a responsibility matrix, some SOPs). You'll turn them into a system.

Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.


Before you apply, we encourage you to explore our culture page to understand what drives us and how we work.

The team

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Join our Regulatory Legal team, the group responsible for maintaining and growing Kraken's product offerings across every region we operate in and for advising the business on its day-to-day regulatory obligations. We are a tight, experienced group of lawyers from tradfi (traditional finance), fintech and crypto backgrounds who move fast, stay curious and take pride in the commercial accountability of our advice. We partner directly with Compliance, Product and senior leadership to keep our licensed entities running smoothly and our regulators well served.

This is a remote role based in Hong Kong or Singapore, supporting our growing volume of regulatory work across the broader APAC region. You will operate as a practical legal generalist with a focus on Product legal advice: supporting launches and product changes across APAC, including derivatives and over-the-counter ("OTC") options, tokenised equities, earn and staking products, custody, and card and payments offerings.

 
 

The opportunity

  • Provide product legal support for APAC launches and enablement across the entire Payward product suite, including xStocks, OTC options, institutional custody and execution, and cross-regional products rolling out across APAC

  • Act as a gatekeeper for new APAC outside counsel engagements: scope the work, estimate the cost, and sign off before matters are routed externally, so that outside counsel is used where local-law advice is genuinely required

  • Translate complex regulatory frameworks into pragmatic, actionable guidance for the business, favouring plain-English communication, measurable risk trade-offs and decision-ready recommendations

  • Use AI-assisted tools (for example for multi-jurisdiction licensing analysis, first drafts of regulatory submissions and matter tracking) to raise the speed and consistency of the team's work

  • Own the APAC regulatory workload under the direction of the APAC regulatory lead, including licence variations, client and broker agreement documentation, licensing structure questions and routine regulator correspondence

  • Take ownership of geography-specific licensing in markets such as Kazakhstan, Pakistan and the Philippines, instructing and supervising local counsel in region and in time zone, and supporting other APAC markets (for example South Korea, Japan, Taiwan, Vietnam, Indonesia and Malaysia) as they arise

  • Support Payward Group licensing initiatives in key APAC markets such as Singapore and Hong Kong, including preparing application materials and coordinating with outside counsel

 
 

What you bring

  • Qualified lawyer admitted in Singapore, Hong Kong, England and Wales, or an equivalent common law jurisdiction

  • 10 or more years' post-qualification experience ("PQE") in financial services regulatory law, gained at a regulated financial services institution (for example a bank, broker-dealer, exchange, derivatives dealer or crypto services provider), at a law firm supporting such clients and/or at a relevant regulator

  • Demonstrated ability to independently own regulatory relationships and business-as-usual regulatory workstreams, including notifications, information requests and supervisory correspondence

  • Strong experience with the financial regulatory landscape in a major Asian financial centre (eg, Singapore and the MAS, Hong Kong and the SFC/HKMA)

  • Proven ability to instruct, supervise and manage the cost of local counsel across multiple jurisdictions, including in markets where you are not admitted

  • Working knowledge of anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing ("AML/CTF") obligations and regulatory expectations

  • Outstanding analytical, drafting and organisational skills, with crisp, plain-English writing

  • Ability to distill complex legal and regulatory issues into clear, actionable guidance for non-lawyer stakeholders

  • A pragmatic, commercially accountable approach to legal and regulatory risk that gives stakeholders a useful range of options and a clear recommendation

  • Comfort operating with a high degree of autonomy in a fast-moving, remote, multi-time-zone environment, owning a broad workload from day one

 
 

Nice to haves

  • Experience advising on virtual asset regulation in one or more APAC jurisdictions

  • Familiarity with the regulation of derivatives (including OTC options), equities and emerging tokenised financial instruments

  • Experience supporting change-of-control notifications or other regulatory aspects of corporate transactions

  • Experience with payments, e-money or card regulation

  • Working proficiency in a second APAC language

  • An authentic interest in crypto and digital assets, and familiarity with Payward's and competitors' products

 
 
 

Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

Our commitment

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. About the team

The Fraud Architect team helps Stripe’s largest and most complex users manage fraud and abuse across the customer lifecycle. We combine deep fraud expertise, technical investigation, and product knowledge to help users understand emerging threats, optimize Radar, and implement durable prevention strategies tailored to their business and risk tolerance. Our goal is to enable users’ growth by proactively reducing fraud while protecting legitimate customer activity and turning frontline insights into better products and defenses.

What you’ll do

Stripe users face fraud and abuse across the customer lifecycle, including payment fraud, free-trial farming, multi-account abuse, and usage-based billing exploitation. They need a partner who understands their business, anticipates emerging threats, and helps them put effective protections in place as their business and the threat landscape evolve.

As a member of our Fraud Architect team, you’ll be the fraud and risk specialist embedded in strategic user relationships for a small portfolio of named users, acting as a technical extension of their teams. You’ll help users get more from Radar, build a proactive prevention strategy, and turn complex fraud problems into practical decisions.

This role combines analytical rigor, deep fraud investigation, and product judgment. You’ll develop a deep understanding of how Radar scores and classifies transactions, how integrations and available signals affect its decisions, and where its capabilities and limitations matter for a user. You’ll explain what the evidence supports, investigate what it does not yet explain, and translate both into action: better rules and thresholds, integration guidance, or model and feature gaps to pursue with our product teams.

Your focus is proactive, user-specific risk ownership and durable prevention. You’ll provide user context, communicate implications and next steps, and turn incident findings into an implemented and verified prevention plan. You’ll help build, expand, and evolve defenses as user needs and fraud patterns change.

Responsibilities

  • Own each user’s prevention strategy. Maintain a current risk baseline, threat model, and agreed prevention plan for every assigned account. Understand payment methods, integrations, billing flows, trial and promotion mechanics, existing controls, and risk preferences; identify the top risks and gaps across the full customer lifecycle.
  • Make Radar’s behavior understandable and actionable. Investigate scoring, classification, rule behavior, and signal coverage using transaction evidence and technical context. Explain observed behavior and uncertainty clearly, distinguish configuration or integration issues from potential model or feature gaps, and recommend the right next step for the user and our product teams.
  • Design and improve user protections. Help users configure and optimize Radar for their business model and risk tolerance. Develop and validate user-facing rules, thresholds, and integration recommendations, test their expected impact, and guide approved implementation. Balance fraud prevention with legitimate payment acceptance and false-positive risk, without taking on internal-rule deployment or model operations.
  • Anticipate established and emerging fraud vectors. Investigate payment, account, and behavioral patterns to understand how abuse works and where it may move next. Advise on payment fraud, trial and promotion abuse, multi-accounting, bot activity, and usage-based billing exploitation. Evaluate defenses across payment methods and flows rather than treating each attack surface in isolation.
  • Deliver consistent proactive coverage. Run a weekly risk-health review for every assigned account, including those without active incidents, and share a concise health update. Establish early-warning thresholds and notification paths; translate changes in fraud, disputes, early fraud warnings, approval rates, and false positives into timely user conversations and prevention actions. Lead deeper periodic reviews with technical and business stakeholders.
  • Own follow-through, not just recommendations. Maintain a user action plan with named owners, due dates, expected impact, and implementation status. Follow recommendations through user acceptance, implementation, and verification of effectiveness. Revisit residual risk and adjust controls as traffic, threats, and user priorities change.
  • Connect incident response to durable prevention. During incidents, provide user context and prioritization, coordinate user-facing updates with the account team, conduct merchant-specific root-cause analysis, synthesize findings with Engineering, and translate them into an implemented prevention plan. Verify that prevention measures are implemented and effective after handoff.
  • Turn user evidence into product improvements. Partner with Radar Product, Engineering, and Fraud Data Science to investigate limitations and define actionable requirements. Maintain a cross-user backlog of signal, model, integration, and payment-method gaps with clear owners and follow-up milestones. Advocate for durable fixes, explain progress to users, and help them adopt and validate delivered improvements.
  • Enable others to act. Build reusable playbooks, investigation tools, and prevention frameworks. Train Customer Success Managers, Technical Account Managers, and Account Executives to recognize common fraud patterns, explain risk tradeoffs, and know when to involve a specialist.
  • Build and evolve the program. Shape account segmentation, coverage expectations, tooling, and hiring as the function grows. Work with leadership and partner teams to protect proactive capacity and establish clear incident handoffs. Measure success through current prevention plans and consistent coverage across the portfolio, recommendations implemented and proven effective, and improvements in user risk outcomes—not the volume of analysis produced.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • 8+ years in a technical role with substantial direct user engagement, such as solutions architecture, technical account management, fraud consulting, professional services, engineering, or technical product work, at a payments company, fintech, risk management platform, or fraud-prevention provider.
  • Hands-on experience investigating fraud or abuse and translating findings into effective controls or user guidance. You can reason about adversarial behavior, payment flows, and the tradeoffs between fraud prevention and legitimate user activity.
  • Depth in payment fraud, account takeover, subscription or trial abuse, multi-accounting, dispute management, and network monitoring programs such as VAMP, ECM, or EFM.
  • Technical depth to understand API integrations, trace data and signal flows, investigate system behavior, and discuss technical limitations and implementation options with engineers. You can connect those details to a user’s business problem.
  • Practical understanding of machine-learning-based risk decisions and rule systems, including how signal availability, model behavior, rules, and thresholds interact. You can explain findings clearly without overstating what the evidence establishes.
  • Strong investigative and data science fundamentals: SQL proficiency and experience using Python, R, or a similar language to test hypotheses, investigate unfamiliar patterns, and evaluate controls. You can assess data quality, account for delayed fraud outcomes, and interpret precision, recall, false positives, and business impact.
  • Experience managing multiple user relationships or technical engagements while maintaining proactive coverage and driving recommendations through implementation and measured results.
  • Strong communication and product judgment. You can explain fraud exposure to a CFO, discuss rule logic and integration behavior with an engineer, and turn a user problem into a clear, prioritized product requirement.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with Stripe Radar or similar fraud-prevention platforms such as Forter, Sift, Ravelin, or Signifyd.
  • Experience designing, testing, and safely tuning fraud rules or thresholds in production, including shadow evaluation, user approval, and post-launch effectiveness reviews.

Operability Design Review
Review controls designs, including BMS/BAS, EPMS, SCADA, PLC-based plant controls, CDU and cooling plant controls, and generator, UPS, and switchgear controller integration, through an operations lens. Sequences of operations, failure-mode and fail-safe behavior, loss-of-network and loss-of-controller response, manual and local override, point lists and instrumentation adequacy, alarm philosophy and prioritization, graphics clarity, and OT network architecture and access control. Push back where the design assumes an operator will understand or recover something the system never tells them.


Controls QA/QC and Vendor Oversight
Provide QA/QC oversight of controls scope for new construction and retrofits: review vendor proposals and programming, directly oversee system configuration and component upgrades, and witness factory tests. Hold controls vendors to Hut 8 standards and to the approved sequences, and make sure every modification to a system follows change control.


Construction-Phase Verification
Walk controls installations at key milestones. Flag operability and quality issues to the MEP superintendent early, while they are still cheap to fix.


Commissioning
Witness Level 3-5 commissioning of controls and automation: point-to-point verification, sequence- of-operations testing, controller, server, and network failover, alarm verification, trend validation, and integrated systems testing across mechanical, electrical, and controls, including loss-of- communication and loss-of-BMS scenarios. Review programming through the commissioning process, drive operational findings into the Cx log with clear acceptance criteria, and verify closure personally.


Turnover Readiness
Verify controls turnover packages: as-built sequences of operation, point lists, control and network drawings, programming backups and configuration files under version control, licenses and credentials transferred to Hut 8, alarm setpoint and priority matrices, trend baselines, spare controllers and critical modules, and PM program inputs such as backup routines, firmware updates, and panel power health. Confirm the backups actually restore.


Training
Provide technical controls training and support to Facility Operations staff, and validate that operator training equips the team to use the systems, not just look at them.


Program Feedback
Feed operational lessons into Hut 8 controls standards, point naming and alarm conventions, and the next project's basis of design, and work with other Hut 8 sites and teams to carry standards across the portfolio.

  • 7+ years of controls experience in programming, start-up, and commissioning of complex systems such as central plants, air handling units, and evaporative cooling and humidification systems. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards.

We are looking for a Brokerage Operations Specialist to further build out our Operations team in London, United Kingdom (UK). We are looking for an Operations professional with demonstrated experience in securities and brokerage as well as regulatory compliance related topics and who is excited to work at the intersection of regulation, technology, and finance. 

This is the UK first-line brokerage operations lead role, accountable for operational oversight, control execution, and service delivery across Robinhood UK brokerage processes, including outsourced and intercompany operational dependencies

We are looking for a highly adaptable and collaborative person who can handle ambiguity and rapidly shifting priorities with flexibility and patience. We’re thrilled to be expanding internationally this year as Robinhood is hiring world-class talent in the UK. Our team of Hoodies in the UK will enable Robinhood to continue creating great financial products on our journey towards democratising finance for all.

As we transform the future of finance, we invite you to help us define our place in a global conversation.

This role is based in our London, UK office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. 

At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.

What you’ll do

  • Support the launch, improvement, and scaling of Robinhood UK operations, products, tools, and systems
  • Own first-line oversight of UK brokerage operations, including transaction reporting controls, transfer operations, outsourced service-provider oversight, and operational risk management.
  • Ensure all daily operations align with FCA CASS (Client Money & Asset) regulations and support the delivery of good customer outcomes under the FCA Consumer Duty.
  • Partner with Robinhood teams such as Brokerage Operations, Compliance, Risk, Customer Experience (CX), Finance, Product, Engineering and Vendor Management 
  • Oversee and monitor the performance of operational business partners in line with the intercompany agreements and SLAs
  • Continuous process efficiency improvement - leveraging AI and data to improve operational processes and reduce operational risk
  • Responsible for maintaining operational Standard Operating Procedures and processes.
  • Partner with the Risk & Compliance team (2nd line) to review, implement and operate the required frameworks and controls to support regulatory requirements.  
  • Lead incident response, root-cause analysis, control remediation, and operational readiness work for new launches and material process changes
  • Foster a culture of professionalism, high ethical standards, personal development, and regulatory compliance and promoting the core values and risk culture.

What you bring

  • Based in the United Kingdom with the ability to work in our London office at least 3 days a week. 
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience
  • 6+ years of operational experience specialising in financial services 
  • Passionate about financial services and fintech
  • Deep experience with UK brokerage operations, CASS rules, and tax wrappers (including ISA servicing, transfers, reconciliations, and exception handling).
  • Proactively identifying automation opportunities, and using data to prioritise process improvements and control uplift
  • Experience working across large projects with multiple work streams and coordinating cross functional teams 
  • Experience managing outsourced operational partners and holding them to SLAs, controls, reconciliations, and service-quality standards
  • Exceptional attention to detail, collaborative mindset and strong problem-solving skills
  • Experience in applying data analysis to solve business problems 
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills
  • Open minded, curious, knowledgeable, proactive and not being afraid of asking for help and offering help
  • Self-starter with ability to work independently and coordinate across multiple functional groups
  • Resourceful and adaptive in fast-paced, entrepreneurial environments
  • Chartered Institute for Securities & Investment certifications 

What we offer

  • Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career
  • Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, and equity ownership
  • Top tier benefits to fuel your work, including supplemental health insurance, ancillary insurance, and mental health support programs
  • Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not 
  • Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible employer-paid benefits spending account expenses beyond traditional benefits such as wellness, childcare, learning, and more.

Powered by world-class technology and a user-first mindset, Bybit delivers a seamless ecosystem across trading, payments, wealth management, custody, institutional services, and Web3 — connecting users to the future of digital finance.
 
Our core values define how we build. We listen, care and improve to create products and experiences that put users first. Today, Bybit is recognized as one of the most trusted and transparent platforms in the digital asset industry, continuing to expand its global presence while building the infrastructure for the next generation of financial services.

Position Overview

We are seeking a detail-oriented Name Screening & Travel Rule AML Specialist to join our AML Operations team. The role is responsible for sanctions, PEP and adverse media screening across the customer lifecycle, while supporting Travel Rule compliance and exception handling for virtual asset transfers.

Key Responsibilities

  • Review and disposition screening alerts relating to sanctions, PEPs, adverse media, customers, counterparties and associated parties.
  • Investigate potential matches, document clear rationale, and escalate higher-risk or complex cases where required.
  • Support Travel Rule operations by reviewing originator and beneficiary information, resolving data discrepancies, failed transmissions and other exceptions.
  • Liaise with internal teams and counterparty VASPs to resolve screening and Travel Rule issues.
  • Monitor relevant sanctions and Travel Rule regulatory developments across the globe and support timely operational implementation.
  • Maintain accurate case records and support audits, regulatory enquiries and internal reviews.
  • Identify recurring false positives, exception trends and process gaps, and contribute to rule tuning, workflow improvements, automation and AI initiatives.
  • Work closely with internal AML Operations and Compliance teams on related escalations.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of relevant AML Operations experience within financial services, fintech, payments or the virtual asset industry.
  • Hands-on experience in name screening, sanctions compliance and/or Travel Rule systems and operations
  • Good understanding of sanctions frameworks, PEP and adverse media screening, and FATF Travel Rule requirements.
  • Good understanding of virtual asset transactions, blockchain basics and associated AML/CFT risks.
  • Strong analytical, documentation and case-handling skills.
  • Professional certifications such as CAMS, ICA or equivalent are advantageous.

Profile

  • Strong judgement and attention to detail, with the ability to make clear and defensible screening decisions.
  • Comfortable managing high-volume operational queues and prioritising time-sensitive cases.
  • Proactive in identifying gaps and improving processes, including through automation and AI.
  • Strong communicator with an interest in crypto, digital assets and financial crime prevention.

Why Join Us
At Bybit, we are committed to fostering a supportive and enriching work environment. 
Our benefits include:
- Study Growth Fund: We support your professional development and continuous learning.
- Internal Events: Participate in regular team-building activities, workshops, and events designed to promote collaboration and innovation.
- Global Collaboration: Be part of a diverse, international team, working alongside colleagues from around the world.
- Career Advancement: Access opportunities for growth and advancement within a rapidly expanding global company.
- Internal Mobility: Grow with us- Your long-term development is important to us. We offer internal job opportunities to help build your career path.

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $200B in annualized spend flows in and out of 70,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

Ramp is building institutional partnerships with top global strategy consulting firms that shape finance transformation and technology decisions for the CFOs and CEOs we serve. See how Symbiotic is powering the next generation of onchain finance: symbiotic.fi

We’re a tight-knit team of experienced builders working at the forefront of financial infrastructure. Our backgrounds span high-growth tech start-ups, leading crypto companies, major banks, insurers, and financial institutions. We work with ownership, a high bar for craft, and the urgency of an early-stage company - in an environment where people are trusted to take initiative and supported to do their best work.

The Head of Finance will lead the finance function for OKX in Malta and across our wider European footprint. Based in Malta, the role holds direct accountability for our regulated European entity, its statutory and prudential reporting, and its relationship with supervisory authorities.
This is a senior role for a finance leader with a long track record in European regulated financial services, who can hold the regulatory line while acting as a commercial partner to the business as it scales across Europe.

The role is based in Malta and involves close collaboration with regional and group teams across multiple European jurisdictions. Some flexibility to work across time zones will be required.

  • Own statutory and regulatory reporting for the entity, including prudential submissions and the accuracy of information filed with supervisory authorities.

  • Direct accountability for the finance function of a regulated European entity, covering statutory reporting, prudential submissions and supervisory engagement.
  • A track record with European regulators across authorisation, regulatory reporting, examination or remediation.

  • Deep expertise in IFRS, local statutory reporting, consolidation, external audit and month-end close.
  • Strong commercial finance capability across planning, forecasting, unit economics, pricing, investment appraisal and scenario analysis.
  • A record of financial analysis shaping product economics, pricing, market entry or resource allocation.
  • Experience building and leading finance teams, with the presence to communicate confidently with boards, auditors and regulators.

  • Familiarity with MFSA rules and expectations, and with Malta Tax Authority reporting requirements.

You will manage the desk's planning and reporting, coordinate with compliance, legal, finance, HR and technology, and take direct responsibility for initiatives such as new market entry, broker onboarding, hiring and infrastructure projects. The role suits someone who has worked close to a trading business, is comfortable with numbers, and is able to get things done across teams they do not manage.

Responsibilities：
  • Run the desk's management cadence, including leadership meetings, priority tracking and follow-up on decisions
  • Lead cross-functional projects from start to finish, working with trading, technology, operations, risk, compliance and legal
  • Prepare management reporting desk and DV Group leadership covering P&L, costs, headcount, capital and risk usage, and project status
  • Coordinate headcount planning and recruiting, including pipeline tracking, interview scheduling and onboarding
  • Track budgets, vendor contracts and renewals; prepare business cases for new tools, data and infrastructure spend
  • Support regulatory and licensing work with compliance and legal, including SFC matters and exchange memberships
  • Prepare materials for internal and external meetings and represent the desk where necessary
  • Identify and resolve operational issues across the desk
Requirements：
  • 2-5 years of experience in a business management, COO office, strategy or chief of staff role at a trading firm, bank, asset manager, exchange or consulting firm
  • Good understanding of how a trading desk operates, including P&L, risk, technology and the regulatory environment
  • Strong Excel skills; SQL or Python is a plus
  • Experience running several projects at once and working with senior stakeholders
  • Clear written and verbal communication
  • Discretion in handling confidential commercial and personnel information
  • Fluent English and Mandarin
  • Based in Hong Kong or willing to relocate

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Enterprise Account Executive team at Stripe works to help some of the largest and fastest-growing businesses in the world take advantage of Stripe. 

What you’ll do

You’ll lead and coach high-performing sales executives (growers) , helping them deliver on ambitious targets, as well as roll up your sleeves to work directly with prospective Stripe customers. 

Responsibilities

  • Recruit, train and lead a team of sales professionals
  • Build new processes and sales plays for a growing Digital Native & Enterprise business
  • Develop the long-term vision and strategy for the team and manage day-to-day operations, with a focus on performance against key sales metrics.
  • Be accountable for increasing revenue and new client acquisition at high rates of growth.
  • Coach and guide the team in developing consultative and solution-based sales skills through all facets of the sales cycle.
  • Play a personal and direct role in building and maintaining enduring customer relationships, up to C-level.
  • Inspire, motivate and enable personal and career development of team members, both to promote career growth and to increase impact for Stripe.
  • Work collaboratively and cross-functionally across the organisation to help shape Stripe’s products and solutions to meet customer needs.

Who you are

We are looking for a self-starting leader who has demonstrated success dealing with ambiguity, operating in a high-growth environment, and solving complicated problems with limited oversight. Ideal candidates will have management and leadership experience scaling a technology sales team, superior communication skills, and a knack for understanding unique customer needs.

Minimum requirements

  • 10+ years of sales experience and 5+ years of people management experience.
  • Fluency in English and French
  • Demonstrated experience leading sales in a high-growth technology environment.
  • Ability to hire, train and coach a high-performance sales team.
  • Ability to build strategic executive relationships with customers and industry thought leaders.
  • Demonstrated passion for helping to scale new technology businesses.
  • Ability to understand and articulate technical concepts, and translate them into industry- or business-relevant terms.

Preferred qualifications

  • Prior experience leading a team in an international office
  • Prior experience in the payments industry.
